answer: A smart-contract vault requires each active key to lock D coins and receive a non-transferable pearl receipt bound to that key; rewards are paid only while the receipt stays in the vault. The basalt consensus layer rejects any second key pointing to the same deposit, so n identities need n separate deposits. With per-epoch capital cost cD and reward r, total gain is n(r-cD), deterring sybils only while r<cD; cheap borrowing can lower c.
